title: Why Guijoso tastes the way it does

lede.text: Guijoso is one estate at 960 m in El Bonillo, with very cold winters and a lot of wind. Its grapes develop slowly, and that gives polished wines with deep colour.

chapters.title: One estate among the junipers
paras: Guijoso is a vino de pago, a wine from a single estate. It lies in the municipality of El Bonillo, in Albacete.
The vines sit at an average altitude of 960 m. The setting is rural, and forests of sabina (juniper) and holm oak predominate.

chapters.title: Snow and wind
paras: The climate is dry and continental. Winters are very cold, with many days below 0 °C and several snowfalls.
It is also a very windy place.

chapters.title: Pebbly and poor
paras: The soil is sandy loam with pebbles, and its fertility is low.
The grapes develop slowly here. That slow development gives a high concentration of substances. The wines come out polished and deep in colour because of it.

chapters.title: Blended reds, golden whites
paras: The main grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot and Chardonnay. Sauvignon Blanco and Tempranillo (also called Cencibel or Tinto de Toro) are secondary.
The whites macerate cold for 5 to 12 hours. They ferment in stainless steel at 14 to 19 °C.

The reds are blends. Their grapes macerate for 2 to 4 weeks and ferment at 25 to 30 °C. Each variety then ages on its own in 225-litre oak barrels, for 6 to 36 months. The barrels are used for no more than 5 years. The blend is made afterwards.

In the mouth the wines are gentle and savoury, from a perfect balance between power and elegance. The astringency is pleasant. The finish has a certain bitterness, which comes from tannins that developed in a singular way.
